mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5% and rises by more than 0.05% in the prior month, it signals tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and rising.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and decline in the unemployment rate signals a strong economy with tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to short-term equity market correction as investors price in higher interest rates over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 6.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when UNRATE > 6.0, the unemployment rate decline fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong consumer confidence and economic activity, which typically translates into higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST growth over the prior month fails to predict positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 over the prior month signals a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 105.0 fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong economic growth regime (GDPC1 > 19000.0), continued expansion in real GDP signals sustained corporate profitability and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 > 19000.0, the signal of strong growth fails to produce positive 20-day SPX returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a robust labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to predict positive 5-day SPX returns in more than 55% of instances.
